codeReview.summary: Passivation options are now threaded through grain identity resolution and execution actors already invoke ctx.Shutdown(), but the feature still falls short of the actor-system contract. On the mission's Windows platform, the retry guard only recognizes a Linux-style bind error, and the added lifecycle tests do not behaviorally prove grain deactivation, retry recovery, or execution-actor disappearance.

issues.description: `isAddressInUseErr` only matches `address already in use`. In this Windows mission environment, a real bind conflict reproduces as `[WinError 10048] Only one usage of each socket address ...`, so `StartActorNode` misses the retry branch at `backend/janus-api/internal/actors/node.go:102-114` and can return an error instead of bumping ports. That makes VAL-AS-016 unreliable on the documented platform.

The new lifecycle tests are mostly structural. They check option counts, helper arithmetic, and non-nil constructors (`TestGatewayGrainOptsWithPassivation`, `TestPortCollisionRetryLoopBumps`, `TestExecutionActorShutdownOnReceive`), but they never wait for a grain to passivate / call `OnDeactivate`, start a colliding second node and observe retry recovery, or assert execution actors disappear after work completes. Regressions against VAL-AS-007 and VAL-AS-017 would likely slip through, and VAL-AS-016 still lacks direct behavioral coverage.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill says actor changes should verify lifecycle behavior via tests, but it does not explicitly warn that lifecycle features need behavioral assertions rather than constructor/configuration checks. This feature was marked as verified even though the added tests never observed passivation, actual retry recovery, or actor disappearance.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared state documents Windows as the platform, but there is no actor-system note capturing that bind-collision errors are OS-specific. That omission makes it easy to implement Linux-only address-in-use detection.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: E:/Janus/.factory/library/environment.md documents Windows as the platform, while backend/janus-api/internal/actors/node.go:510-514 hard-codes `address already in use` matching; a local reproduction in this session returned `[WinError 10048] Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted`.

summary: Fail: passivation wiring and execution-actor shutdown calls are present, but port-collision recovery is not reliable on Windows because the retry guard only recognizes a Linux-style bind error. The added tests are also too shallow to directly validate passivation, retry recovery, and post-execution actor cleanup.
